answer: A farm grew a thousand vertices in a garden, each linked only to the others, hoping the shape passes. A real vertex sits in a garden of links that point outward, each answered back by a stranger, and the farm's plume fans out from one center and never leaves it. A fake vertex needs links from outside, and a thousand fakes need a thousand real relationships. A new vertex looks like a plume at first, so the network gives it time to grow outward before judging it.
